newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SES property index surges 3.11 pct on optimism.
newsitem.headline: SES property index surges 3.11 pct on optimism.

text.p: The property index on the Singapore stock exchanged surged 22.32 points, or 3.11 percent, on Friday afternoon on renewed optimism that the worst might be over for the property market, dealers said.
The property index was at 739.11 at 0745 GMT after touching a low of 718.57 earlier in the day.
City Development Ltd, Keppel Corporation, DBS Land and Singapore Land were the main property counters which led the index up, dealers said. They were all among the gainers.

"These are all index-linked stocks and have been included in major portfolios of big foreign funds, especially from the U.S. and the United Kingdom, on increased expectations of better performances," said one dealer.
The participation of all major developers in recent land auctions in Singapore also helped boost sentiment in the property market, he said.
"There is a belief that the worst might be over for the Singapore property market," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
He said the optimism in the property market was spilling over into banking stocks, which were also among the top gainers.
City Development shares rose Singapore $0.70 to S$13.50, Keppel Corporation was up S$0.60 at S$11.60 and Singapore Land rose S$0.20 at S$8.65.
